correctness.rationale: The four class families reconstruct the same intersection-multiplicity multigraph for every smooth complex degree-two del Pezzo surface. The transformation E↦−K_S−E preserves intersections since (−K_S)²=2 and (−K_S)·E=1. The root-deleted Laplacian M presents the degree-zero quotient in the differences [i]−[r]; the omitted Laplacian column is minus the sum of the others, and T really sends the i-th basis difference to [ι(i)]−[ι(r)]. The critical pairing can be computed by solving Lz=x over the rationals and reducing z·y modulo one, for degree-zero x,y. This gives the perfect reduced-matrix pairing, independent of the additive constant of z, and invariant under the vertex permutation. Thus T−ε is self-adjoint and the annihilator of its image is precisely its kernel; the kernel is abstractly the dual of the augmented cokernel. An independent exact replay reproduced the determinant 2^114·5^7·7^47 at roots 0,1,7,28 and all 24 augmented Smith checks. Minimal-valuation pivots allow invertible row/column elimination over the local residue rings. Each precision exceeds the entire base determinant valuation, so no augmented factor can be hidden by reduction, and no additional prime can enter because the augmented cokernels are quotients. For + the nonzero local valuations are p=2: 1 once, 2 twenty-six times; p=5: none; p=7: 1 twenty-six times. For − they are p=2: 1 six, 2 fourteen, 4 seven; p=5: 1 seven; p=7: 1 twenty-one. Aligning the sorted local diagonals gives Z/2 ⊕ (Z/28)^26 and (Z/2)^6 ⊕ (Z/28)^14 ⊕ (Z/560)^7. Their orders multiply to 2|K|; the minus subgroup exhausts the full 5-primary subgroup. The Néron interpretation uses the equivariant identification with the dual-graph critical group under the explicit nodal, split, regular unit-thickness smoothing assumptions.
residual_risks: The replay computed the two augmented cokernels rather than the kernels directly; the pairing argument is the needed link. No smoothing existence or unweighted-graph result is inferred, and the uploaded verifier was not executed.

evidence: The known curve intersection and pairing specify the matrices in principle. The known ordinary group gives only the Smith form of M; the audited presentation appends T−εI, yielding different integral groups and a product of orders equal to 2|K|.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither invariant factors of M nor rational ± eigenspaces determine the position of the integral relation lattice relative to the involution. The standard pairing reduction is not a new general theorem, but it leaves a nontrivial integral computation specific to the geometric action; neither neighboring group calculation covers that computation.

value.rationale: The full exceptional-curve multigraph and its Geiser involution are canonical geometric data, not a parameter slice chosen after computation. The two integral structures identify exactly what remains fixed and what is negated, giving useful information for equivariant component groups when the smoothing hypotheses hold. In particular, the factor-of-two discrepancy and exact high two-power factors resolve what a rational eigenspace or ordinary critical-group calculation cannot distinguish.
residual_risks: The result does not classify other curve-graph actions, determine the full integral representation up to conjugacy, or establish existence of an equivariant semistable model.
